author: Sakura Murakami
description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung will meet on Tuesday, seeking stronger economic ties amid increasing geopolitical uncertainty set off by the war in Iran and shifting dynamics between the US and China.
title: Japan and Korea Set to Meet Tuesday Amid Iran, China Uncertainty

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Pentagon’s internal watchdog will investigate whether US boat strikes in the Caribbean followed targeting guidelines, amid claims from outside groups that the attacks were illegal.
title: Defense Watchdog Will Probe US Attacks on Boats in the Caribbean

description: Shawn Harris, US House Candidate (D) Georgia, states that kitchen table issues will decide who wins the Georgia primaries this Tuesday. He states that agriculture and farmers are the “center of gravity for Georgia,” and details the various issues people in the state are struggling with. He also talks about supporting the gas tax holiday, and shares his thoughts on the outcome of President Trump’s trip to China. Shawn Harris speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power” live from Atlanta, Georgia. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Farmers Center of Gravity: Harris on Georgia Primary Day

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Vladimir Putin is set to travel on Tuesday to Beijing for talks with President Xi Jinping in his first foreign visit of the year, with the war in Iran offering an opportunity for Russia to deepen energy links with China.
title: Putin Aims to Unlock Gas Pipeline Project to China in Xi Talks

author: Sergio Mendoza
description: Violent clashes in Bolivia intensified with protesters squaring off against security forces as food shortages stoke anger and some opponents of President Rodrigo Paz call for his resignation.
title: Unrest Boils in Bolivia as Some Demand President’s Resignation

description: Rep. Nikema Williams, a Georgia Democrat, says voters understand “what’s at stake” as the state heads into Primary Day, with races from governor and Senate to state Supreme Court seats on the ballot. Williams says voting rights, redistricting and affordability are top of mind for constituents, arguing that housing, gas and grocery costs remain urgent concerns across Georgia. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power” live from Atlanta, Georgia. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Williams: ‘Everything’s Up for Grabs’ on Georgia Primary Day

description: Today, Matt Schettenhelm, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Litigation Analyst, breaks down a California's jury's rejection of Elon Musk's claim that Sam Altman betrayed OpenAI's original mission when it became a for-profit business, finding that Musk waited too long to sue his former company. Then, Dr. Doug Lucas, an orthopedic surgeon who leads the clinical side for bone health and longevity science at LifeMD, joins the show live from the New York Stock Exchange to talk bone health and preventing osteoporosis. Plus, Ed Ludlow, host of Bloomberg Tech, sits down with Dell CEO Michael Dell and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sit down for an interview on the future of computing at Dell Technologies World Conference. Finally, back at the New York Stock Exchange, Dr. Susan Blumenthal, retired Rear Admiral and former US Assistant Surgeon General, discusses the women's health landscape and the economic gains that can come from centering women's care. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Musk Loses Bid to Force OpenAI Overhaul|Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 5/18/2026

description: Allen Fromherz, director of Georgia State University’s Middle East Studies Center, says escalation against Iran is not “fully merited” after President Trump called off a planned strike. Fromherz says Trump appears to be listening to Gulf allies who still see a ceasefire as the best outcome, while Iran is using a strategy of “delay and deflect” in negotiations. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power” live from Atlanta, Georgia. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fromherz Says Iran Escalation Not ‘Fully Merited’

author: Tracy Withers
description: New Zealand will overhaul its public service, including job cuts and mergers between some government departments, as it looks to trim costs, Finance Minister Nicola Willis said.
title: New Zealand to Cut Public Service Jobs, Merge Some Departments in Overhaul

description: President Donald Trump explains why he called off a strike on Iran after an appeal by the leaders of Persian Gulf allies, who called for more time to pursue a diplomatic resolution. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Calls Iran Attack Pause a 'Positive Development'

author: Toru Fujioka
description: A senior Japanese Finance Ministry official sowed doubt over any prospects for the nation to sell US Treasuries as part of any move to prop up the yen, suggesting the maneuver could end up being counterproductive.
title: Japan Official Sows Doubt Over Potential US Treasuries Sales

author: Scott Patterson
description: The Trump administration is poised to roll out a plan for trading digital versions of securities that could reshape the landscape of the American stock market as it continues to loosen the rules for free-wheeling crypto markets.
title: SEC to Ready Plan for Trading Crypto Versions of Stocks

description: On today’s Big Take podcast, host Sarah Holder and Bloomberg’s global trade editor Brendan Murray discuss whether the US-China summit actually reshaped trade relations – and the obstacles that remain. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Where the US-China Trade Relationship Stands Now

author: Courtney McBride
description: The State Department has approved potential sales of up to $4.2 billion in helicopters and related equipment to South Korea, according to announcements Monday.
title: US Approves $4.2 Billion in Helicopters, Upgrades for Seoul

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses Tuesday's primary elections. On today's show, Joe is live from Georgia Tech in Atlanta. He speaks with Georgia Tech President Angel Cabrera, former Atlanta Mayor Shirley Johnson and Grammy Award Winning Rapper Michael "Killer Mike" Render. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Live in Atlanta for Georgia Primary | Balance of Power: Early Edition 5/18/2026

description: A close associate of ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro made his first appearance in Miami federal court after being sent to the US over the weekend to face money-laundering charges.
title: Deported Maduro Ally Charged With Money Laundering in US Court

description: Companies and individuals making deals to settle Securities and Exchange Commission cases no longer have to remain silent after the settlements, the regulator said Monday.
title: SEC Ends Decades-Old ‘Gag Rule’ in Enforcement Settlements

author: Nancy Cook
description: Trump and Republicans are looking for ways to show action on economic concerns.
title: Trump Tries to Regain Some Ground on Affordability Issue

author: Jordan Fabian
description: President Donald Trump requested a federal investigation into unsubstantiated claims that Maryland sent hundreds of thousands of “illegal” mail-in ballots to voters.
title: Trump Calls for Justice Department Probe Into Maryland Voting

description: Chuck Leavell, Rock and roll superstar, member of Allman Brothers, and The Rolling Stones joined Joe Mathieu on Balance of Power to discuss Georgia's upcoming primaries. They also discussed AI and the future of the music industry as well as what issues the people of Georgia are concerned about including the rise in data centers.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: 'People Are Concerned' Over The Data Center Boom In Georgia Says Leavell

author: Alicia A. Caldwell
description: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent was charged with assault by Minnesota authorities for allegedly shooting a Venezuelan man and then lying about the confrontation.
title: ICE Agent Charged in Shooting of Venezuelan Man in Minnesota

description: President Donald Trump’s administration slapped sanctions on some of Cuba’s top leaders and its spy agency, as Washington aggressively ratchets up pressure in a bid to end nearly seven decades of communist rule.
title: US Targets Cuba’s Leaders, Generals and Spies With New Sanctions

description: Michael "Killer Mike" Render, Grammy Award Winning Rapper, Actor, Activist and Social Justice Advocate joined Balance of Power to discuss the Georgia primaries and the importance of getting out to vote. He also discusses Georgia's economy and the future of AI in music.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Redistricting is not Only a Racial Issue Says 'Killer Mike'

description: Ángel Cabrera, President of Georgia Institute of Technology joined Balance of Power on the road in Georgia to discuss the outlook for Higher Education amid economic uncertainty and how AI is impacting the way students are learning in colleges and universities. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: 'AI is Changing Everything' in Higher Education Says Georgia Tech President

description: Former Atlanta Mayor Shirley Franklin joined Balance of Power live from Georgia saying the record turnout for early voting in Georgia shows that voters are paying attention to what's going on in the country and the state and they're deeply engaged. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Georgia Sees Record Early Voting As Primaries Loom

description: Saxby Chambliss, former US Senator from Georgia (R), former Senate Agriculture, Nutrition and Forestry Committee Chairman (2005-07), former Ranking Member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence (2011-12) joined Balance of Power to discuss the Georgia primary race tomorrow and what the voter is really focused on in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The 'Pocketbook' is The Number One Issue For Voters Says Chambliss

author: Lydia Beyoud
description: The White House is reviewing whether to amend and potentially scrap a decades-old rule governing stock trading that’s meant to make sure investors get better prices for their transactions.
title: White House Reviews Ban on Trading Through Best Price on Stocks

author: Laura Nahmias
description: Zohran Mamdani was set to hold individual meetings with Jamie Dimon, chief executive officer at JPMorgan Chase & Co., and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. CEO David Solomon, as New York City’s democratic socialist mayor seeks to build relations with the business community.
title: Dimon, Solomon to Meet With Mamdani as Mayor Pushes Higher Taxes

description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday said his department is issuing a “temporary 30-day general license” allowing the sale of Russian crude oil and petroleum products that are already loaded on tankers. Tyler Kendall reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US to Issue New Russia Oil Waiver as Iran War Hits Supplies

author: Zach C Cohen
description: A string of attacks on synagogues and other Jewish institutions is prompting calls to more than triple the amount of federal assistance they can get to protect their buildings from future attacks.
title: Jewish Group Seeks $1 Billion to Shield Buildings From Attacks

description: Brazil’s Finance Ministry raised its consumer price forecasts sharply and now sees inflation running above target through at least 2027, reflecting the shock from the Middle East war.
title: Brazil’s Government Now Sees Inflation Soaring Past Target for Longer on Iran War

description: The European Union will tie some payouts from the €90 billion ($105 billion) aid package for Ukraine to an unpopular tax change already demanded by the International Monetary Fund, people familiar with the matter said.
title: EU Ties Part of Ukraine €90 Billion Aid to Unpopular Tax Measure

description: Ghana wants large-scale gold mines to sell at least 30% of their annual output to the central bank to increase local refining and boost the country’s foreign-exchange reserves.
title: Ghana Seeks 30% of Large Gold Mines’ Output For Local Refineries

description: Kevin Warsh will be sworn in as Federal Reserve chair by President Donald Trump on Friday during a ceremony at the White House, an official said.
title: Trump to Swear In Warsh as Fed Chair on Friday, White House Says

description: Pitching to succeed Keir Starmer, Andy Burnham invoked the specter of another former British prime minister — Margaret Thatcher — in his bid to win back working-class voters.
title: Burnham Rails Against Thatcher in Leadership Pitch to Labour

description: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said Europe must assert its own interests against global competitors with measures such as favoring companies from the region.

description:
The revolt against Prime Minister Keir Starmer has reignited debate about reversing Brexit — nearly 10 years after the UK voted to leave the EU.

Alex Wickham explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Revolt Against Starmer Reignites Debate on Undoing Brexit

description: The US is expected to issue a waiver allowing the sale of Russian crude oil and petroleum products that are already loaded on tankers, according to people familiar with the matter, just days after the previous one lapsed.

description: Ford Motor Co. is in negotiations with defense departments in Europe and North America to supply pickup trucks and software to their armed forces.

description: Adani Enterprises agreed to pay $275 million over a probe by the Office of Foreign Assets Control, according to the Treasury Department.

description: The US Supreme Court let stand a $194 million award against Eli Lilly & Co. in a whistleblower suit accusing the company of engaging in Medicaid fraud by misreporting its drug prices.

description: The US Supreme Court turned away appeals from six pharmaceutical companies seeking to topple the Medicare drug price negotiation program that’s led to billions of dollars in discounts on top-selling treatments.

description: President Donald Trump moved to drop his $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service over the 2019 leak of his tax information.
title: Trump Moves to Drop $10 Billion US Lawsuit Against IRS

description: Germany is seeking to invest €10 billion ($11.6 billion) to improve civil protection over the coming years, including in additional bunkers and an app to warn citizens about finding the nearest shelter in case of war or natural disaster.
title: Germany Plans to Invest €10 Billion in Civil Protection Measures

description:
Long Island Rail Road riders are bracing for hours-long commutes as a salary fight between the nation’s busiest commuter rail line and its employees forced a systemwide shutdown, the first in more than 30 years.

LIRR customers are scrambling for alternative ways to get to and from New York City and throughout Long Island after the Metropolitan Transportation Authority and union leaders failed to reach a deal by a late Friday night deadline after two days of marathon contract negotiations.

MTA Chair Janno Lieber joins Bloomberg Surveillance Radio to discuss the state of ongoing talks between the agency and unions. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: LIRR Strike Snarls NYC Commutes as Settlement Talks Continue

author: Maciej Martewicz
description: Poland seeks to hold “honest talks” with the US after it was blindsided by Washington’s decision to halt deployment of its troops to the NATO ally, according to Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.
title: Poland Seeks ‘Honest Talks’ With US on Troop Levels in NATO Ally

description: Iran has started a Bitcoin-backed insurance service for shipping companies that want to transit the Strait of Hormuz, the semi-official Fars news agency reported, citing documents obtained from Iran’s Ministry of Economy and Financial Affairs.

description: Group of Seven finance chiefs are meeting in Paris to discuss how oil-fueled inflation risks overshadowing economic prospects. The talks are meant to dwell on imbalances ranging from the US budget deficit to China’s weak consumption. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports from Paris. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: G-7 Ministers to Discuss Inflation, Imbalances, Oil

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, the global bond selloff deepens as rising oil prices fuel inflation concerns. President Trump has warned Iran that the 'clock is ticking' for a deal to be done to end the war, but both sides remain at loggerheads.

Spiking bond yields are likely to dominate a meeting of G-7 finance ministers in Paris, as oil-fueled inflation threatens global growth. The French Finance Minister Roland Lescure tells Bloomberg the bond market is correcting rather than collapsing.

Today's guests: Seema Shah, Principal Asset Management, Chief Global Strategist; Roland Lescure, French Finance Minister. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trumps Says Clock is Ticking for Iran | Daybreak Europe 05/18/2026

author: Daniel Flatley
description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on the G-7 nations and others to increase sanctions on Iran as the conflict that has snarled a large portion of the global energy trade drags on without an end in sight.
title: Bessent Calls on G-7 Nations, Others to Increase Iran Sanctions

description: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure discusses the European economy, the risk of inflation and rising bond yields. Speaking to Bloomberg's Oliver Crook on the sidelines of a meeting between Group of Seven finance ministers in Paris, he says the European economy is "proving quite resilient."  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lescure Says European Economy 'Proving Quite Resilient'

description: The French economy should return to growth in the second quarter and avoid a recession this year, Finance Minister Roland Lescure said.

title: Trump Filing Reveals Stake in Sushi Chain Alongside Big Tech
